note: Rust: fixed window per client IP, /api paths only. First request of an IP opens its window; the window never rolls until a request arrives at or after start+window (lazy). allowed = ++count <= limit; remaining = limit - count saturating at 0; reset = (window - elapsed) in whole seconds. Defaults limit 300, window 900 s (std-http-server sets the same). ORB_DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT=1 disables. 429 body: text/plain, 'Too many requests, please try again later.'. Headers on EVERY /api answer (admitted and denied): ratelimit-policy '<limit>;w=<window>', ratelimit-limit, ratelimit-remaining, ratelimit-reset. No retry-after, no x-ratelimit-*. A request with no peer address or a path outside /api is not counted. Cases use limit 3, window 10 s for brevity; std-rate-limiter is configured requestsPerMinute 3, windowSeconds 10. std ticks are wall-clock and not stepable, so std rolls the window with WINDOW_ELAPSED and the golden resetIn mid-window is checked on the Rust side only.

std.atom: std-rate-limiter-ip (trait RateKeyRateLimiter), composed by std-http-server as ServerRateLimiter; the single shared bucket atom std-rate-limiter stays for apps that count one bucket (std-api-gateway).
std.key: ip from the router: the peer ('ip:port' from std-http1 REQUEST_RECEIVED) with the last ':port' dropped; carried on RATE_REQUEST { requestId, ip }. An IPv6 peer keeps its brackets (a key, not a parsed address).
std.eviction: none; Rust RateWindows never removes an entry either.
std.result: replayed with orb execute --steps: all expectations hold (steps 1-6 as above; the ip-less request is uncounted).

timeDerived.newWindow: time/now - windowStart >= windowSeconds*1000 opens a fresh window at that request (count 1)
timeDerived.evaluated: orb evaluate on windowStart = now - 0/4000/9999/10000/12000 ms (each call lags ~1 s of process start): reset 9,3,-5,-7,-11 and roll false,false,true,true,true; the rolled cases are the path where the arm resets instead of reporting reset. --steps cannot seed an entity or move the clock, so the t=4 and t=10 Rust rows are covered by this expression check, not replayed end to end.
